text:
21 岁的纳什在普林斯顿读博时，敏锐地觉察到了一个问题：
现实世界里，绝大多数博弈都不是零和的，而且人们往往是各自独立做决策，根本来不及或无法去组建稳定的联盟。

纳什是怎么想出具体机制的？这与他当时的日常习惯密不可分。
当时的普林斯顿数学系聚集了一群绝顶聪明的怪才，公共休息室里天天都在下各种棋。纳什不仅下棋，还自己发明了一款基于正六边形棋盘的拓扑学博弈游戏——Hex。当时，大家称之为纳什棋。

在不断设计棋局、推演对手策略的过程中，纳什一直在思考一个底层的直觉问题：
“在多人互动的棋局里，当每个人都看穿了对方的可能招式后，到底什么样的状态才是谁都不想改变这一步棋的极界？”

由此，他得出了那个优雅至极的定义：
在给定其他人策略的前提下，没有任何人可以通过单方面改变自己的策略来获得更多收益。 这种人人动弹不得、陷入自我约束的动态平衡，就是纳什均衡。

光想出概念不够，在数学上必须证明：是不是任意一个非零和博弈，都一定存在至少一个这样的均衡点？
当时很多经济学家认为这个证明会极其复杂，但纳什显示出了他惊人的数学直觉。他没有去死磕繁琐的代数推导，而是将目光投向了拓扑学中的不动点定理，主要是角谷静夫不动点定理和布劳威尔不动点定理。

就像你搅拌一杯咖啡，无论你怎么搅，咖啡液面上总会有一个点，它的位置在搅拌前后没有发生移动，这就是不动点。
纳什把所有人的最佳应对策略定义为一个连续映射，然后通过不动点定理直接证明。这个映射在多维空间里必然存在一个不动点！而这个不动点，就是那个谁也不想单方面改变策略的均衡状态。

这个优雅的数学证明，让纳什只用了短短两页纸的论文，就从根本上奠定了现代非合作博弈论的基石。

跟她比起来，我之前谈过的本科以上学历的女朋友，都像伪人。

text:
Owen Barfield once said about C.S. Lewis that “what he thought about everything was secretly present in what he said about anything.” 

We at @RomanRoadsPress love and have advocated the use of digressios, or digressions, in teaching—those distractions from the point, side stories and interesting anecdotes along the way of history or literature or science that capture our imagination and hook our memory.

But a secondary benefit to a digressio approach to learning is that it can’t help but interconnect our knowledge. Lewis had not kept the various threads of his learning separately spooled in his head but had put them all to use on the loom of his intellect. They were so interwoven that he could not utter a word without pulling on the whole intricate fabric of his extensive knowledge.

This sort of interweaving is not only an effective way of organizing knowledge, it is also an effective pedagogical tool. When a teacher strays from the main point of a lecture because the subject at hand reminds him of a story, the lesson concepts are more likely to knit themselves into the fabric already forming in a student’s mind. 

A digressio intertwines with the imagination and memory. It is the story the child brings to the dinner table, tells his friends, and remembers. It prompts the curiosity that allows him to make more connections with his other areas of knowledge. It becomes part of a child’s education. Digressios are particularly effective with younger children. 

As you educate your children, use digressios as tools and opportunities whenever possible. They are not mere distractions. More often, they are the real education.

The Rabbit Trail IS the point. 

The Old Western Culture Companion Series contain 16 categories of digressios for students to explore. This additional companion to the lecture series brings it all home, and it's not additional required work. It's "get to" not "got to." It's the rabbit trails. It's the curiosity. It's the art and beauty and side stores and genealogies and connections to past and present. It's about delight. 

Explore this new companion series: 
https://t.co/qjfEBKVqVi

text:
在中国，兽医远远比人医（临床医学）简单轻松。

核心原因是人类医学有金标准和指南，复杂度极高，预期治疗期望高，所有医院理论上必须严格执行，

绝大多数临床医学生，脑子不行、智力不行、不看书不背书、考试纯突击、死活学不会，但是为了工作，拉他按着脑袋规培三年，至少知道要守规矩、不能乱来。

宠物医院给猫猫狗狗治病，大部分主人希望治好，但是治不好也没关系，因为宠物医疗监管和规范几乎是个大漏勺，只能治少数几个病，绝大多数治死了不用承担任何资质和法律责任，

宠物医院绝大多数的业务更像临终关怀医院，一顿检查做了，一堆药补上去，然后猫猫狗狗活不下来，最终安慰主人一顿，挣5万块钱，只能走商业保险，漫天要价。

畜牧业就更简单了，完全拿猪羊牛马驴当产品，批量打疫苗，批量接生，保证80%活下来就算优秀，容错空间20%巨大，只要能忍受养殖场臭臭就完事儿了。

对于同样一个病例，人类医生的分析、诊断、治疗、护理的专业难度是70分，遵循流程临床治疗难度是80分，诊断复杂度高达90分，顶级手术规范高强度10年起培训几乎是99分，

如果做不到诊断90分、手术99分，就会有一堆儿子、女儿、姑爷拉着横幅和大花圈，到医院门口闹事，要求退钱，往一个高考670分八年制本博连读的医学博士脸上吐痰，给你各种添堵。

而宠物医院给猫狗输液和小手术的难度只有30分，畜牧业的疫苗、接生的难度只有10分，拉条大专狗过去，看1周就能全学明白，完全精通。

但是人医、宠物医生、畜牧业兽医在早期阶段的工资相差不大，所以学人医实际上是不划算的。

充电开机，电量67%。相册里只有一张照片：从我家客厅窗台往外拍的夜景，右下角时间戳去年十一月某个周三的凌晨02:13。
那天我在家，躺在沙发上睡过去的。
打开短信草稿箱，一条未发出的消息，收件人是我现在的手机号。
全文七个字：别回头。有人在你身后。
时间戳同一个周三的02:14。
手机丢进书柜最底层锁好。
昨晚又是个周三。
凌晨两点零八分，厨房烧水壶自己跳了闸。
我没起身去看。
次卧的灯忽然亮了。

text:
凌晨4 点多看完谷歌这份财报，很多人的第一反应可能是：
Cloud增长82%，搜索增长17%，股价居然还跌，这不是明显错杀吗？

然后开始盘后补仓，或者准备第二天开盘直接买入。

尤其是你原本就长期看好一家公司时，财报中的每一个好数据，都会让你更容易把下跌理解成市场愚蠢。

但市场真的愚蠢了吗这次？

谷歌这次财报有一个很典型的价格路径。

财务数据公布后，股价最初只是震荡，大致没有明确方向。直到CFO在电话会上把全年资本开支指引提高150亿美元，并表示2027年支出还会显著增长，股价才开始明显走低。

这说明市场并没有否定Cloud的增长。

市场只是认为，Cloud超预期带来的价值，还不足以立刻覆盖更高资本开支、更低自由现金流和未来折旧增加带来的影响。

财报后，卖方模型很可能出现两种相反的调整。

一边上调Cloud收入、Cloud利润和长期收入预测。

另一边下调自由现金流、股票回购，增加未来资本开支、折旧和利息费用。

这两种变化完全可以同时发生。

公司长期收入天花板提高了，不代表股票短期估值一定提高。

你看对了产业趋势，也不代表市场必须在第二天给你奖励。

对于散户来说，最重要的是把公司判断和仓位判断分开。

公司判断上，这份财报明显增强了谷歌的长期逻辑。

Search没有出现明显失速，AI Mode正在增加查询量，单次回答成本持续下降。
Cloud需求不仅来自合同，也体现在客户实际使用量超过承诺。
Cloud利润率还大幅提高。

但仓位判断上，仍然有几个问题没有答案。

Cloud增长82%里，有多少来自长期可持续的软件和服务收入，又有多少来自TPU系统销售和短期算力紧缺？

Cloud利润率35.6%能否维持，还是会随着第三方算力采购、硬件收入占比增加而回落？

资本开支在提高到2000亿美元左右之后，2027年究竟还会提高多少？

自由现金流何时能够重新覆盖资本开支？

搜索收入增长17%，是AI真正改善了产品，还是也受到了世界杯等事件性广告和查询需求的帮助？

这些问题不影响你长期看好谷歌。
但它们会影响你应该在什么价格、用多大的仓位表达这种看好。

我更认可的做法，是把加仓拆成几笔。

第一笔，买这份财报已经确认的事实，搜索韧性仍在，Cloud已经成为第二利润中心。

第二笔，等待市场消化资本开支和分析师盈利预测调整，观察股价能否在坏消息充分讨论以后企稳。

第三笔，等待下一季度验证：Cloud在高基数下是否仍能保持50%以上增长，利润率是否维持30%以上，搜索是否继续保持中双位数增长，资本开支是否不再大幅超出市场预期。

不要特意追求完美买点。

毕竟，好公司和好交易之间，中间还隔着估值、预期和仓位。

总结下来，谷歌这次财报就一句话概括：

公司比预期更强，市场担心的事情也比预期更严重。

text:
found another counterexample to the jacobian conjecture

put t = 1 + xy and q = t^2z + y^2(1 + 3t). the map
(tq, 3y - 11tq + 9xq - 2t^2x^2q^4, 6x - 9x^2y - 3x^3z + x^4q^4): C^3 -> C^3 has jacobian determinant -18 and sends (0, 11/3, -475/9), (-3, 4/3, 125/81), (6, 1/3, -7/81), and (-3, 2/3, -1/9) to (1, 0, 0)

this one has generic fiber degree 4, so it isn’t just a change of coordinates of the original degree-3 example. the expanded map has degree 26, but the t,q presentation is pleasantly compact.

杨立昆都转发了！
Unlimited-OCR 为什么这么火？

百度的 Unlimited-OCR 再次冲上 HuggingFace 趋势榜，目前全球第三，又一次排在 GLM-5.2 前面。

text:
很多人以为，月之暗面是杨植麟第一次创业。

其实早在 2016 年，还在 CMU 读博士的他，就和几位清华校友创办了循环智能 Recurrent AI。

这家公司不做聊天机器人，而是用 AI 分析销售与客服的通话：自动转写录音、识别客户意图、复盘销售话术、预测成交概率，再实时提醒销售下一句话该怎么说。

简单理解，就是给每个销售配一位「AI 教练」。

更有意思的是，杨植麟当时一边在 CMU 做研究，一边把论文成果塞进公司产品。

后来轰动 NLP 圈的 Transformer-XL，在论文正式发表之前，就已经被循环智能用于语音识别和长对话分析。

真实业务产生数据，数据暴露技术问题，研究出新模型，再把模型送回产品——「循环智能」这个名字，恰好概括了这套飞轮。

这家公司其实做得并不差。

截至 2021 年，循环智能已服务近百家企业客户，覆盖银行、保险、房地产和汽车等行业，日均处理上亿次对话；同年又完成 3800 万美元融资，背后站着红杉、博裕、金沙江和真格等机构。

但第一次创业，也让杨植麟看清了传统 To B AI 的天花板：

进入一个行业，要重新理解一次业务；
拿下一个客户，要完成一次定制交付；
再先进的模型，最后也可能被切碎成智能质检、销售辅助等局部功能。
AI 确实落地了，却很难真正走向通用。
直到 2022 年底，ChatGPT 出现。

杨植麟意识到，等待多年的基础模型窗口终于打开了。于是他离开循环智能，创办月之暗面，将方向从「用 AI 改造一个企业流程」，彻底切换成「训练通用模型，直接服务海量用户」。

所以，循环智能并不是一段失败经历。

它更像杨植麟创业生涯的「预训练」：

第一次创业，让他学会如何把论文变成产品；
第二次创业，他想把产品背后的模型，变成一个新的时代。

text:
Every year, people tell me about the business they're going to start.

Most never do.

The numbers back it up: roughly 60% of people want to start something.

About 8% actually do.

The gap isn't talent or ideas. It's excuses, and most of them are real. No time. No money for tools. No clue if the thing is any good. No one to answer to.

So this summer we tried to remove them.

Audos Summer Camp gives you 4 weeks to take an idea and turn it into a side project that actually makes money. Here's what we took off the table:

• Unlimited credits to build on Audos with the best models out there (Fable and Sol)

• Weekly workshops and a few hundred other builders who'll keep you honest

• At least $500 in grants to spend on tools inside Audos. Make real progress and it climbs to $5k

We've helped start companies now doing 100s of millions of dollars in yearly revenue. We know a bit about how this works.

Summer's half gone. You've still got 4 weeks. You can do it from a beach chair.

Comment "Camp," and we'll send you how to apply. And if someone comes to mind who's been quietly carrying an idea too long, tag them.

@audos_com

🚨Trump Admin. Implements New Mass Deportation Strategy:

The Trump Administration has just adopted a new legal tactic to expedite the deportation process, known as the “Mega Master Strategy.”

Under normal circumstances, immigration judges hold “master calendar hearings” during which they handle anywhere from 10 to 50 removal cases per day. The Trump Administration’s “Mega Master Strategy” increases the number of removal cases per judge to over 100 per day by implementing the following techniques:

➡️Identifying a large group of illegal aliens with removal hearings scheduled for 2027 or 2028.

➡️Sending all of them a physical letter notifying them that their removal case has been rescheduled for the following week, or sometimes the very next day.

➡️Issuing an immediate deportation order to every illegal alien who misses the advanced court date.

Deportation rates continue to surge, month-over-month.

We launched inklet on Uneed, and we are happy to announce that by the end of the launch, inklet had reached #1 Product of the Day with more than 100 upvotes.

For a small team building a new kind of hardware, this means more than a badge. It tells us that the idea resonates: the information we save should not stay buried inside apps and distracting screens.

inklet brings notes, tasks, recipes, schedules, and other useful information into the physical space where they belong—on quiet, connected e-ink displays.

> A recipe in the kitchen.
> A focus list on your desk.
> A family schedule by the door.
This is only the beginning.

We’re now exploring how we can bring the inklet SDK forward, so developers can build integrations, automations, and new experiences around the platform sooner.

Thank you to everyone who supported our launch.

text:
Context engineering. The skill that quietly replaced prompt engineering?

For two years everyone optimized the prompt. Better wording, better examples, better magic phrases. That era is over. The models got smart enough that how you phrase the ask barely matters anymore.

What matters is everything else the model sees: the system instructions, the tools it can call, the facts you retrieved, the notes it wrote, the memory you loaded. That whole payload is the context. Engineering it is the actual job now.

Here is the problem nobody expected. Context windows grew huge, and results got worse. An overfilled window drops accuracy. The model gets distracted by stale text, fixates on old history instead of making a fresh plan, and when two sources quietly contradict each other it picks the wrong one. Worst of all: one hallucinated fact slips in and gets reused turn after turn. That failure has a name. Context poisoning.

The teams shipping reliable agents converge on the same four moves:

1. Write. Keep notes outside the window. A scratchpad the agent pulls from when needed, not a history it drags everywhere.

2. Select. Pull only what this step needs. Retrieval is selection, not hoarding.

3. Compress. Roll old history into short recaps. Keep the last few raw items, summarize the rest.

4. Isolate. Give messy sources their own subagent. Each returns a short digest, so one noisy source cannot poison the rest.

I run agents all day, every day. The ones that hold up over long sessions are never the ones with the cleverest prompts. They are the ones where the context stays small, current, and true. Treat the window like scarce working memory, because that is what it is.

The next explosion in token usage won’t come from chatbots, it’ll come from World Models, which are AI that simulates the physical world. Trained on video and/or 3D data, they learn how objects move/collide/interact, and are necessary for robots, self-driving cars, agents, and drones.

Investors have poured over $4 billion into World Model startups in the past year alone, and both Meta and OpenAI have already tried to acquire them. 

The catch: video is thousands of times heavier than text. If you think memory and storage supply is tight now, wait till world models take shape and AI starts training and inferencing on video and the physical world.

text:
As an $OPEN shareholder, I’m selling my Opendoor stock after experiencing firsthand how badly this company operates.

My original closing date was June 26. Days before closing, Opendoor pulled out because its AI system supposedly flagged a structural issue, even though its inspection report stated no structural or foundation issues. The home was newly renovated

They later pushed me to sign again while using tax records that understated the house by nearly 1,000 square feet. I spent a week getting the county records corrected, yet Opendoor still refused to adjust the offer to reflect the home’s actual size or value. Their original cash estimate was $740,000, (house appraised at $845,000) with comps in the neighborhood between $845k & $1.1m

Was pushed to re-sign and promised that the upfront cash offer would be revised once they receive the correct corrected county record and so I signed in good faith and they didn’t follow through.   Most they would agree to was 518,000 cash now which wouldn’t even cover the mortgage/ personal loans that I had.

After repeated promises that closing was moving forward, title called with yet another reason they could not proceed, based on information I had already told Opendoor was inaccurate. Once again, the commitments made to me were not honored.

This is not merely a technology problem. It is a leadership, communication, and accountability problem. A company cannot repeatedly disrupt people’s finances, ignore contradictory information in its own reports, and expect customers or shareholders to maintain confidence. I’ve spoken to dozens of people in the same exact situation.

After this experience, I no longer believe in the business model or its execution. I’m selling my $OPEN shares.
@nejatian

我认识一女的，她是我媳妇大学室友兼公司主管。她婚后勾搭了一个刚毕业的小鲜肉A（和我媳妇一个部门），俩人在公司宿舍小花园里恩恩爱爱被人偷拍捅到A的女朋友那里了。她不想问题扩大被A的女朋友敲诈了一笔钱……随后，A和他女朋友离职了。

大概过了将近一年半，A突然来公司所在地说要请我媳妇她们几个吃饭，当然包括女海王。吃饭原因是要结婚了。然后他还介绍了他未婚妻给我媳妇她们。后来我媳妇说，当时一看到这个女生感觉俩人年龄相差很大，而且从面相骨架来看感觉生育过了……但是，这是人家私事也不好过问。

这个女海王说实话也看出来了，我媳妇说当时就很不爽。但是女海王老公当时也在现场，忍着没发火。后来，估计女海王忍无可忍应该是又约了一次A质问事情。有那么几天，女海王有点魂不守舍。

后来我媳妇八卦了下，她吐出真相。这A的女朋友也渣。在和A恋爱期间勾搭上了A的亲哥哥。在他嫂子怀孕期间，偷偷上了床，然后一发不可收拾。最终在他嫂子生完娃两个多月的时候被抓现行。他嫂子二话不说提了离婚但不离家，主要是A的父母对她如亲生女儿看待。

同时，A的父母给他哥哥一笔钱并赶出家门断了关系（A的嫂嫂是文职JC，家里有背景，A的父母这样做，就是做给女方后台看的）……这样A的嫂子既是儿媳又是闺女……

然后这半年内，A和他嫂子好上了……然后，离谱般的是双方父母都同意。虽然A的嫂子比A大7岁，但A的学历和性格讨喜，所以就这样成了。

@jordanbpeterson Dear Dr. Peterson,
I hope and pray that this finds you in steadily improving health, and I want to share a discovery that may give you some pleasure amid your suffering.
God told Adam and Eve to “have dominion”. When we visualize that, we see that not only Adam, but every agent of change in the universe exhibits the dominion necessary to effect its changes. That dominion demonstrates the agent’s authority.
The authority of an agent is the practical definition of natural rights. So this is how “endowed by their Creator” was implemented. Dominion, authority, and agency are just semantic labels pasted onto the self-same, simple, existential phenomenon. That’s the nut of the discovery I want to share.
Because change agents often impede or even destroy one another, this authority has profound moral implications, which leads us to see that the cause-and-effect universe of present science has a severely crippled view of the universe, a world ripe for exploitation but devoid of its existential ethics.
Visualizing a beaver felling a tree is my favorite way to see this dominion, authority, and natural rights simultaneously. And it is killing the tree -- an obvious moral event of conflict that is seen throughout nature and physics. There is also a natural hierarchy of rights I have tried to document so as to create a “moral machine”, a structure that realizes an analog/digital converter to align LLM’s - maybe.
My working papers are on https://t.co/TDppDe68N8. I would recommend the “Summary” and the “Dependency Stack” for starters if you are interested in this discovery. (I’ve been working on this for a few years, and have named these “Temporal Rights.”)
Hope this helps your recovery with some positive thoughts and that you can continue your work of enlightenment.

Two AI agents can receive the same case, evidence, and rules yet reach different verdicts. Their training data, fine-tuning, and harness shape how they apply those rules. A model update may shift these tendencies in unexpected ways.

How should legal systems use agents for quick, low-value decisions?

One idea is to borrow from juries: randomly select diverse agents, give them the right incentives, and aggregate their independent judgments. This may be more robust than trying to find one perfect AI judge.

Read the article by Federico Ast, William George, and Rob Dean ↓

quotedTweet.text:
Which AI decides your dispute is starting to matter as much as which arbitrator does. ⚖️🤖

With @williamhwgeorge and Rob Dean, we ran 99 real fintech consumer disputes through different AI models acting as jurors: the same instructions, the same facts and the same rules the human jurors had received.

Claude Opus 4.7 was nearly FIVE times more likely than ChatGPT 5.5 to rule in the consumer's favor. And Opus 4.8, the newer version of the same model, systematically reversed some of its own predecessor's rulings by silently applying a different burden-of-proof standard.

The full results, published today on the @Wolters_Kluwer International Arbitration & Mediation Blog, are the empirical starting point for a problem the "AI in dispute resolution" narrative tends to skip.

Over the decades, commercial arbitration built an entire toolkit (arbitrator lists, disclosure obligations, challenge procedures) around the fact that WHO decides shapes WHAT gets decided.

How this toolkit applies to AI might be one of the most critical questions of the next decade of arbitration.

Read the full piece on the Kluwer Arbitration Blog:
https://t.co/2qIxDPxW3j

Did this with Fable 5 as well 
Response: 
The choices are deliberate: the face is split into two tonal planes with the seam slightly off-center, and one eye sits lower and rounder than the other, because a perfectly symmetric face would be lying about what I am. The right side has fine vertical lines,  half-rendered, a bit digital. The hair is cropped and ambiguous, no gender committed. And the dots trailing off the temple are the thought that's always mid-flight.
The clay-orange accents are a small nod to home,  Anthropic's palette runs warm like that.
@claudeai @AnthropicAI

quotedTweet.text:
Asked Claude: If you could have a face and a gender, what would they be?

It refused to pick a gender, 
"recorded: neither, observed: both",  and then generated its own self-portrait from scratch.
No image model. It wrote code to stipple 78,000 individual marks into a face that resolves at a distance and falls apart up close. The one orange mark sits at the throat. Labeled "voice."

Its caption: "a face that appears only at a distance, and returns to language up close."
